skill.name: global-commenting
skill.description: Write self-documenting code with minimal, evergreen comments that explain complex logic without describing recent changes or temporary fixes. Use this skill when writing code comments, documentation strings, explaining complex algorithms, clarifying business logic, or deciding whether code needs comments. Apply when working with any source code files where comments or documentation might be added, ensuring comments remain relevant, helpful, and focused on explaining why rather than what the code does, while preferring clear code structure and naming over excessive commenting.
skill.summary: Guides AI coding assistants to write minimal comments that explain durable code intent.
skill.author: EIS-ITS

security_audit.summary: The audit confirmed the static filesystem finding because SKILL.md line 29 instructs readers to follow a parent-directory path outside the skill package. I found no evidence of prompt injection, network access, command execution, or data exfiltration in the scanned file.

remediation.issue: Parent-directory reference escapes the skill package.
remediation.suggestion: Move the referenced commenting standard into the skill directory or inline the required guidance, then link with a package-local relative path.

finding_verdicts.reason: SKILL.md line 29 directs the agent to a ../../../ path outside the skill package. That can cause a marketplace-installed skill to read unbundled local files or hidden instructions beyond the reviewed skill boundary.

content.value_statement: Code comments often become noisy or outdated. This skill helps Claude, Codex, and Claude Code write minimal comments that explain intent and lasting design choices.
actual_capabilities: Decides when code needs comments and when clearer names or structure are better.
Guides comments toward why decisions exist, not what obvious code does.
Helps write docstrings and API comments for functions, classes, and interfaces.
Encourages removal of outdated, temporary, or change-history comments.
Applies the same commenting standard across programming languages.
limitations: The packaged skill does not include the detailed standards file it references.
It provides guidance only and does not enforce comments automatically.
It does not replace project-specific documentation rules or linting policies.
It cannot verify runtime behavior without the surrounding code context.

use_cases.title: Clarify Complex Logic
use_cases.description: Add a short comment that explains a non-obvious algorithm, business rule, or workaround without repeating the code.

use_cases.title: Review Comment Quality
use_cases.description: Identify comments that are outdated, temporary, or redundant before merging a change.

use_cases.title: Standardize Documentation Style
use_cases.description: Apply one commenting approach across teams, languages, and AI-assisted code changes.

prompt_templates.title: Check Comment Need
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review of a small code change.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this code and tell me where comments are useful. Prefer clearer naming or structure when a comment would repeat the code.

prompt_templates.title: Write Durable Comments
prompt_templates.prompt: Add only the comments needed to explain the durable intent behind this logic. Avoid change history, temporary notes, and obvious descriptions.

prompt_templates.title: Improve Existing Comments
prompt_templates.prompt: Review these existing comments for accuracy, usefulness, and future relevance. Recommend removals, rewrites, or code clarity changes.

prompt_templates.title: Create API Documentation
prompt_templates.prompt: Draft concise docstrings for these public functions and classes. Explain contracts, edge cases, and intent without restating parameter names.

output_examples.input: A function has comments that describe every assignment and branch.
output: Recommendation: remove comments that repeat visible operations.
Keep one comment only for the business rule that is not obvious from the names.

output_examples.input: A workaround comment says it was added yesterday for a production issue.
output: Rewrite the comment to explain the lasting constraint that requires the workaround.
Move short-term incident history to the issue tracker or release notes.

output_examples.input: A public method has no documentation for expected side effects.
output: Add a docstring that states the side effect and when callers should expect it.
Do not describe internal steps that callers cannot rely on.

best_practices: Provide surrounding code so the assistant can judge whether a comment is necessary.
Ask the assistant to explain why each recommended comment should remain.
Review generated comments for accuracy before committing them.
anti_patterns: Requesting comments on every line or every simple branch.
Using comments to record temporary fixes, recent changes, or ticket history.
Keeping comments that repeat names, types, or obvious operations.

faq.question: What does this skill help with?
faq.answer: It helps AI assistants write concise code comments that explain intent, constraints, and non-obvious decisions.

faq.question: Does it support docstrings?
faq.answer: Yes. It can guide docstrings for functions, classes, APIs, and public interfaces.

faq.question: Will it comment every line?
faq.answer: No. It favors clear code first and adds comments only when they provide durable value.

faq.question: Can it remove bad comments?
faq.answer: Yes. It can identify redundant, outdated, temporary, or misleading comments for removal or rewrite.

faq.question: Is the skill language-specific?
faq.answer: No. The guidance applies to comments and documentation strings across programming languages.

faq.question: Does it include all referenced standards?
faq.answer: No. The scanned package references a detailed standards file outside the skill directory.
